this government ask for training and other operations to be available to all those men and women across this country who lose their jobs as a result of this deal? No, it does not. Let us be clear. This government is opening up the door to the transnational companies. They are not companies in Canada trading with a company in the United States or with a company in Mexico. It is the same company just trading within itself. That is the kind of trade that most of our companies are into. It is saying that it is going to open the doors and make it easier for companies to move that part of their operation which is labour intensive into Mexico or into the southern United States. That is what we are talking about and that is why we, as New Democrats, oppose this legislation so strongly.

Madam Speaker, what Canada needs is a fair set of rules, fair trading agreements and agreements that will create jobs here in Canada. That is not what Canadians have received. It is clear that two-thirds of Canadians oppose the NAFTA. It is incomprehensible to this side of the House why the government insists on pushing through the deal this week. I ask the Deputy Prime Minister: What kind of commitments has this government made? It wants to push the legislation through this week when it has not even been completed in the United States and, indeed, is not even completed. Has this government made specific commitments and if so, to whom? To the Prime Minister of Canada? To the United States? To the international business community? What are the commitments this government has made that necessitate ramming this through this week?

Madam Speaker, my question is for the Minister of National Health and Welfare. Perhaps the minister will listen carefully to my question. Last week the chair of the subcommittee on poverty admitted to having sent a staff member to masquerade as a poor person and intercept several bags of food from the Daily Bread Food Bank intended for the genuinely poor. The same member told this House that the poor should be taught how to live with less food while her staff is busy pillaging the little food they still have. Will the minister explain why his government permits its Oral Questions poverty chief to carry out this kind of guerrilla attack on the food supply of the poorest of Canadians?

I can only repeat what I said in my answer to the hon. member's first question. NAFTA and the free trade agreement have nothing to do with increased importation of illegal drugs, other than allowing our well-trained officers the opportunity to have more time, more resources, more technology and a greater effort in dealing with missing children, the importation of illegal drugs, illegal firearms and other illegal substances into Canada. Since the free trade agreement has come into effect, we have improved and increased our seizures of illegal drugs coming into Canada. That trend will continue with the signing of the NAFTA agreement.
